title: Guided onboarding checklist — step brainstorm + doc link map (Phase 1: Hosted API)
body:
Context
- Phase 1 scope = Hosted API (self-serve). We need a guided checklist in Console that reduces time-to-first-success (TTFS) and clarifies the minimal path to a safe “first production launch”.
- This doc is a working brainstorm to:
  1) propose checklist steps + ordering
  2) map each step to a canonical docs URL (or placeholder)
  3) note which steps can be validated automatically vs require manual attestation

Assumptions / constraints
- We should keep the initial checklist short enough to feel finishable (~6–10 steps). Consider “Basics” vs “Production readiness” grouping.
- Validation is strongest when it’s based on server-side signals (gateway logs/metrics) rather than client-only.
- Telemetry collection constraints (initial position):
  - NO prompt or completion content
  - prefer allowlisted properties only (ids, timestamps, status codes, model id)
  - avoid collecting raw error messages; use normalized error codes
- Console deep links should be stable and versionable; we will likely need redirect support in docs.

Proposed step groups (working)
A) Get a successful response (activation)
B) Use core features safely (streaming/structured output/tools)
C) Make it production-ready (retries/timeouts, quotas, observability, safe rollout)

Step list (v0 brainstorm)
NOTE: Titles are rough. We’ll need final microcopy in a separate copy doc.

1) Create an API key
- Why: unblock first call; reduce 401 tickets.
- Suggested Console CTA: “Create API key” (deep link into API Keys page).
- Definition of done:
  - at least one API key exists for the org OR project (TBD)
- Validation: AUTOMATIC (Console action or backend key create event)
- Candidate telemetry:
  - onboarding.api_key_created { key_type: test|prod (if available), project_id?, org_id }
- Docs link (placeholder): https://docs.redwoodinference.com/docs/getting-started/api-keys
- Notes:
  - Support tickets suggest confusion between environments; we probably need to split “test” vs “prod” key later (see step 6).

2) Install an SDK (or call the REST API)
- Why: reduce friction + ensure consistent retries/timeouts defaults.
- Definition of done:
  - user chooses a language + sees the snippet (this step may be “completion by view” only)
- Validation: SEMI-AUTO (we can mark complete when user selects language + copies snippet; but “SDK installed” is not verifiable)
- Candidate telemetry:
  - onboarding.sdk_option_selected { sdk: python|typescript|go|curl }
  - onboarding.code_snippet_copied { snippet_id }
- Docs link:
  - Python: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/docs/sdks/python
  - TypeScript: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/docs/sdks/typescript
  - Go: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/docs/sdks/go
  - REST/HTTP: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/docs/api-reference
- Notes:
  - Keep one canonical snippet per language used across Console + docs + quickstarts.

3) Make your first request (non-streaming)
- Why: primary TTFS milestone.
- Definition of done:
  - first successful 2xx response for the project (generation/chat/embeddings acceptable?)
  - “success” should be based on gateway logs, not client reporting
- Validation: AUTOMATIC (server-side)
- Candidate telemetry:
  - onboarding.first_successful_request { project_id, endpoint: chat|responses|embeddings|rerank, http_status: 200, model, region }
- Docs link:
  - Quickstart (single canonical): https://docs.redwoodinference.com/docs/quickstart/first-request
- Open questions:
  - Should embeddings count as “first success” or do we require a generation/chat response?
  - Do we want to require “model selected from catalog” first?

4) Try streaming (recommended)
- Why: streaming is common; also where many disconnect issues occur.
- Definition of done:
  - successful streaming session with at least N chunks delivered (TBD)
  - handle disconnect edge case (don’t mark complete if session fails before first token)
- Validation: AUTOMATIC (gateway/stream metrics)
- Candidate telemetry:
  - onboarding.first_streaming_session { project_id, endpoint, completed: true|false, disconnect_reason?: normalized }
- Docs link:
  - Streaming guide: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/docs/guides/streaming
- Notes:
  - We should include a quick “streaming troubleshooting” link from the checklist.

5) Structured output OR tool/function calling (choose one)
- Why: most app developers need one of these; but forcing both may be too much.
- Proposed behavior:
  - Checklist step is “Optional but recommended” OR “Pick one path”
- Definition of done:
  - user indicates they shipped either structured output or tools OR we detect API usage (if possible)
- Validation: MIXED
  - Automatic if we can detect request parameter usage (e.g., response_format / tools array) from allowlisted request metadata
  - Otherwise manual attestation (“I tried this”)
- Candidate telemetry:
  - onboarding.used_structured_output { project_id, schema_type?: json_schema|regex|other }
  - onboarding.used_tool_calling { project_id, tool_count }
- Docs link:
  - Structured output: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/docs/guides/structured-output
  - Tool calling: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/docs/guides/tool-calling
- Privacy note:
  - If validating via request metadata, ensure we do NOT capture schema contents/tool definitions—only booleans + counts.

6) Create a “Production” API key (separate from test)
- Why: avoid mixing dev/test keys in production and reduce 401 + permission confusion.
- Definition of done:
  - at least one key labeled prod exists
- Validation: AUTOMATIC if we add prod/test labeling to key system; otherwise MANUAL until key UX exists.
- Candidate telemetry:
  - onboarding.prod_api_key_created { project_id, org_id }
- Docs link:
  - Keys & environments: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/docs/getting-started/environments-and-keys
- Notes:
  - Support request: “wrong key in prod” is a frequent issue. This step is likely high impact.

7) Add retries + timeouts (minimum resilience)
- Why: prevent outages and reduce avoidable support tickets; this is a “production readiness” foundation.
- Definition of done:
  - hard to validate; best is to provide SDK defaults + highlight config options
  - consider a checkbox attestation: “Configured timeouts and retries in production path”
- Validation: MANUAL (Phase 1) unless SDKs can emit a safe signal.
- Candidate telemetry:
  - onboarding.retries_timeouts_attested { sdk, project_id }
- Docs link:
  - Retries/timeouts guide: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/docs/guides/retries-and-timeouts
- Notes:
  - If SDKs ship sensible defaults, we can shift this from “do this” to “verify defaults / override as needed”.

8) Understand rate limits & quotas (and how to handle 429)
- Why: 429 during onboarding is a common frustration; we should preempt it.
- Definition of done:
  - user visits quota settings OR docs; optional: user sets a budget/limit (future)
- Validation: SEMI-AUTO
  - automatic: “visited quota page”
  - manual: “I implemented 429 backoff”
- Candidate telemetry:
  - onboarding.quota_page_viewed { project_id }
  - onboarding.rate_limit_docs_viewed { project_id }
- Docs link:
  - Rate limits: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/docs/platform/rate-limits
  - Quotas & usage limits: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/docs/platform/quotas
  - 429 handling: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/docs/troubleshooting/429-rate-limited

9) Set up observability basics (usage + errors)
- Why: production launch should include visibility into spend + failures.
- Definition of done:
  - user visits usage dashboard OR sets up basic logging/tracing hook
- Validation: SEMI-AUTO (page visit) for Phase 1
- Candidate telemetry:
  - onboarding.usage_dashboard_viewed { project_id }
  - onboarding.error_dashboard_viewed { project_id }
- Docs link:
  - Usage analytics: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/docs/console/usage
  - Debugging errors: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/docs/console/errors
  - Request IDs & tracing hooks: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/docs/guides/observability
- Notes:
  - We should ensure request IDs are prominent in SDK examples + docs (helps support).

10) First production launch (final milestone)
- Why: makes “done” concrete and measurable.
- Definition of done (candidate):
  - has prod key + retries/timeouts + quota awareness + basic monitoring + rollback plan
  - may include a “soft launch” (limited traffic) concept
- Validation: MANUAL ATTESTATION (Phase 1). Potentially “guided form” inside Console.
- Candidate telemetry:
  - onboarding.first_production_launch_attested { project_id, checklist_version }
- Docs link:
  - First production launch checklist: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/docs/guides/first-production-launch
- Open questions:
  - What is the minimum bar we’re comfortable calling “production launch”?
  - Should we explicitly include “canary rollout” or “fallback model” in Phase 1, or keep as best practice?

Mapping table (condensed)
Format: Step → Canonical URL → Validation level
- Create API key → /docs/getting-started/api-keys → Auto
- Install SDK / REST option → /docs/sdks/* and /docs/api-reference → Semi (view/copy)
- First request → /docs/quickstart/first-request → Auto
- Streaming → /docs/guides/streaming → Auto
- Structured output / tool calling → /docs/guides/structured-output OR /docs/guides/tool-calling → Mixed
- Prod API key → /docs/getting-started/environments-and-keys → Auto (once key labels exist)
- Retries + timeouts → /docs/guides/retries-and-timeouts → Manual (Phase 1)
- Rate limits + quotas → /docs/platform/rate-limits + /docs/platform/quotas → Semi
- Observability basics → /docs/console/usage + /docs/guides/observability → Semi
- First production launch → /docs/guides/first-production-launch → Manual

Validation signal source brainstorm (what’s feasible)
Auto (good candidates)
- API key created (Console/backend)
- First successful request (gateway logs/metrics by project_id)
- First streaming session (gateway stream metrics)
- Prod key created (once key labeling is shipped)

Semi-auto (OK candidates)
- “Visited usage dashboard” (Console page view event)
- “Visited quotas page” (Console page view)
- “Copied snippet” (Console client event) — NOTE: easy to game but still useful for funnel analysis

Manual attestation only (Phase 1)
- Configured retries/timeouts appropriately
- Implemented structured output schema correctly (unless we can detect request params safely)
- “Ready for production” composite step

Open questions / decisions needed
- Step ordering: do we put “rate limits” earlier (before first request) to avoid early 429 frustration, or later to avoid overwhelm?
- “First success” definition: should embeddings count? (affects TTFS metric and validator)
- Project vs org: checklist state likely should be per project; but API key is often org-wide. Need consistent language.
- Docs URL versioning: should Console link to “/docs/…” (latest) or “/docs/v1/…”? We’ll likely need stable permalinks + redirects.
- UTM conventions: likely need utm_source=console&utm_medium=checklist&utm_campaign=guided_onboarding&utm_content=<step_id> (TBD; coordinate with Design/PM)

Next actions (who)
- Elliot: propose initial docs IA + create placeholder pages/redirect plan for the canonical URLs above.
- Monica/Ibrahim: confirm SDK snippet parity plan and whether we can detect structured output/tool calling without logging content.
- Nadia/Logan: sanity check which validation signals can come from gateway metrics vs request logs, and expected lag.
- Marissa/Dylan: confirm Console can emit “page viewed” events in a privacy-safe way and support step state persistence.
